concepts.def: Multicultural society — over 25% of Germans have a Migrationshintergrund (migration background).
Largest minority group; descendants of Gastarbeiter who arrived from 1961 onwards.
Official statistical category covering people who themselves or at least one parent were born without German citizenship.
Disputed concept of a 'guiding culture' to which immigrants should adapt.
Weak, strong, mixed endings depending on article: 'die neue Heimat, ein neues Land'.
Discrimination — banned by the Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz (AGG) of 2006.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Multiculturalism in German-speaking Society — a core area of A-Level German.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Multiculturalism in German-speaking Society brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Multiculturalism in German-speaking Society.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: When does 'in' take the accusative vs dative?
options: Nominative.
It always takes the same case.
Accusative for movement INTO a place; dative for location IN a place.
It depends on the speaker's mood.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I watch TV every evening' in German?
options: Ich sehe jeden Abend fern.
Nominative.
Ich fernsehe jeden Abend.
Ich sehe fern jeden Abend.

mcqs.q: What case does 'helfen' (to help) require for its object?
options: It depends on the speaker's mood.
Nominative.
Dative - 'Ich helfe DIR' (I help you).
Accusative - 'Ich helfe DICH'.
